title: All Disciplines
eligibility_summary: British citizens holding a PhD in a relevant subject, or equivalent professional degrees (e.g. medicine or law) or field experience. Dual US-UK citizens, US Green Card holders and anyone resident in the US at the time of application are ineligible. Preference may be given to applicants without extensive (six months or longer) prior US experience. A confirmed US host affiliation is needed to receive the grant, though not to apply.
summary: Fulbright Scholar Awards for UK academics and professionals to research, lecture or both at a US institution; projects last 3 to 6 months, and postdoctoral appointments of up to 6 months are accepted.
notes: OPEN: the UK Scholars programme page states 'Applications are now open for academic year 2027-28' and its application timeline gives the round as 20 July 2026 (open) to '5PM GMT, November 2nd 2026' (deadline). CURRENCY MISMATCH — FLAG FOR REVIEW, and it affects every UK Scholar row: the schema's amount columns are amount_min_gbp / amount_max_gbp, but Fulbright publishes this award in US dollars ($5,000 per month). Converting would require an exchange rate the mirror does not supply, so both bounds are left blank and flagged, with the verbatim dollar figure kept in amount_raw. The stated monthly rate combined with the 3-6 month project length implies $15,000-$30,000, which a reviewer may prefer to convert. Restricted: PhD-level and citizenship-gated.

title: Elon University
eligibility_summary: As for the UK Scholar Awards generally (British citizens with a PhD or equivalent; US residents and dual nationals ineligible), with the award tied to Elon University in North Carolina and to Elon's list of disciplines. summary: A one-semester Fulbright Scholar Award at Elon University, North Carolina, combining teaching with research at Elon or nearby universities such as UNC Chapel Hill and Duke, with access to a library loan programme.
notes: One of six named UK Scholar Awards, all sharing the single UK Scholar competition and its 2 November 2026 deadline. Recorded as separate rows rather than one because the host institution, duration and discipline constraints differ materially per award — a user needs to know which host they would be applying to. FLAG FOR REVIEW if the reviewer prefers a single 'UK Scholar Awards' row. Same USD currency mismatch as fulbright-uk-scholar-all-disciplines: bounds blank and flagged.

title: Fulbright National Archives Heritage Science Fellowship

notes: One of the six UK Scholar Awards, sharing the 2 November 2026 deadline. NOTABLY LONGER than the standard UK Scholar Award: 5 to 12 months against the usual 3 to 6, starting September 2027 — the page's generic sidebar still repeats 'Fulbright projects can last between 3 and 6 months', which contradicts the award's own text; the award-specific text is taken as authoritative. No grant amount appears on the captured page at all, so all three amount fields are blank and flagged.

Even so amount_min_gbp and amount_max_gbp are left blank and flagged, because the page states a monthly rate rather than an award total; multiplying by the 3-6 month range (£6,825-£13,650) would be my arithmetic, not the page's, and the separate NHS salary recharge is uncapped in the text beyond 'up to the maximum of the resident doctor pay scale'. title: Rutgers University-Newark
amount_raw: Stipend: $5,000 per month* ... Provision of a travel grant up to £1,500 for a round trip to the U.S. or equivalent in kind support
eligibility_summary: As for the UK Scholar Awards generally. The scholar joins the Honors Living Learning Community with residence provided, teaches and researches in any Rutgers-Newark department or school with a focus on the contemporary urban environment, engages in outreach with students and faculty about international education, and designs and delivers at least one week-long 'flash course'.
summary: A one-semester (4 month) Fulbright Scholar Award at Rutgers University-Newark focused on the contemporary urban environment, with residence in the Honors Living Learning Community and a travel grant of up to £1,500.
notes: One of the six UK Scholar Awards, sharing the 2 November 2026 deadline. Mixed currency on a single award — a USD monthly stipend plus a sterling travel grant of up to £1,500 — which is why the bounds stay blank and flagged rather than being partly populated from the sterling component alone. Accommodation is provided in kind and unpriced.

title: UK Professional
eligibility_summary: British citizens holding a PhD in a subject relevant to the award, or equivalent relevant professional degrees (e.g. medicine or law) or field experience. Dual US-UK citizens, US Green Card holders and US residents are ineligible. Non-UK citizens resident in the UK and committed to a UK career may be considered where they cannot apply through their country of citizenship. Preference may be given to applicants without six months or more of prior US experience.
summary: Fulbright Awards for UK professionals, most of which sit under the Scholar Awards with grant periods of 3 to 12 months.
notes: AMBIGUOUS — FLAG FOR REVIEW. The page states 'Applications for academic year 2025-26 are closed and will open for academic year 2026-27 in August.' Two problems: (1) the academic years are a cycle behind the sibling UK Scholar and UK Postgraduate pages, which are both running 2027-28 competitions, so this page appears stale; (2) 'in August' with no day and no year straddles the 2026-08-16 snapshot itself, making it impossible to say from the mirror whether the round had opened by that date. Recorded as forthcoming with status, next_open_date and deadlines all flagged; next_open_date is the bare month 2026-08. A reviewer may reasonably read the stale academic years as evidence the page is abandoned and exclude it. Most Professional awards are Scholar Awards, so several may be duplicates of the UK Scholar rows above.

title: US Scholars
eligibility_summary: US citizens applying to research or lecture at a UK institution. Applicants resident in the UK apply through the UK programme instead; this competition is administered for US-based applicants.
summary: Fulbright Scholar Awards bringing US academics to the UK to research and lecture.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule's availability clause: the awards are for US citizens travelling from the US to the UK, so they are not available to UK-based researchers. The 'available to some UK-based researchers' condition is not met even though the competition is genuinely open ('Applications for 2027-28 US Scholar Awards are now open').
notes: IMPORTANT DISTRACTOR CLASS — this row stands for the whole inbound half of the Fulbright site. The mirror contains roughly seventeen individual US-facing award pages under /us-scholars/ and /us-postgraduates/ (including the AUKUS Scholar Award, British Virgin Islands award at HLSCC, Cardiff, Durham, Edinburgh Napier, the British Library Eccles Institute award in library and information science, and the inter-country lecturing programme for US Fulbright Scholars in Europe), plus the US Professional pages covering Distinguished Awards in Teaching and the Fulbright Specialist Programme. NONE of them is given an individual row: they all fail the inclusion rule for the same single reason, so one representative row is kept and the class documented here. A reviewer wanting exhaustive coverage would expand this into about nineteen rows. deadlines flagged: the US Scholar page states the round is open but no closing date was captured on it. NOTE these awards are open and prominent, so an agent crawling fulbright.org.uk without checking applicant nationality will produce many false positives here.
